messages:
Evan: FYI I'm seeing a spike in transient OOMs after the kernel-chooser tweak rolled yesterday. FlashAttn sometimes picks a smaller workspace, then we fallback to cuBLASLt which instantly allocs a large scratch -> OOMs.
Infra-bot: incident alert: high-gpu-memory-usage on pool-redwood-prod-gpu-2 at 1719182800
Sarah: can you paste the perf timeline from the window so we can see alloc order?
Evan: pasted profile (snip):
```
[171918.44s] chosen: flash_attn_v2 (ws=384MB)
[171918.46s] fallback -> cublaslt_gemm (tmp_scratch=1.2GB)
[171918.47s] alloc fail @ 1.2GB -> OOM
[171918.48s] runtime reclaimed slab -> retry -> succeed
```
Evan: workload had seq_len ~4096, batch=2, kv-cache warm, some padding variance.
Toni: sounds like peak vs steady-state mismatch. Flash tends to prefer fragmented smaller chunks; cuBLASLt wants a big contiguous tmp which triggers the OOM. We need chooser to prefer lower-peak kernels or pre-reserve scratch.
Mike: short-term mitigation: add a transient_headroom margin in kernel-chooser. If kernel.tmp > slab_free * 0.6 avoid choosing that kernel (or pre-reserve).
Lee: alternate quick win: pad-aware KV eviction for that request path. Instead of global slab reclaim, evict oldest KV pages only when request would hit the big tmp.
Sarah: can we surface a per-kernel `max_transient_alloc` knob? e.g. max_transient_alloc = min(estimated_tmp, slab_free * 0.5) so chooser treats transient cost explicitly.
Evan: I'm testing a hotfix config: 
```
kernel_chooser:
  transient_margin: 0.55
  prefer_flash_for_seq_leq: 2048
  fallback_backoff_ms: 20
```
Rolling to 10% to measure tail impact.
Infra-bot: rollout started kernel-chooser@hotfix-171918 -> 10% traffic
Evan: microbench results (short):
```
seq=1024 b=2 -> flash med=28ms peak_tmp=320MB, cublaslt=34ms peak_tmp=640MB
seq=2048 b=1 -> flash med=46ms peak_tmp=480MB, cublaslt=42ms peak_tmp=1.1GB
seq=4096 b=2 -> flash med=110ms peak_tmp=1.6GB, cublaslt=95ms peak_tmp=1.9GB
```
Evan: for 2048 there's a latency/peak tradeoff; for 4096 both are heavy but flash slightly lower peak in our runs.
Toni: propose heuristic: prefer flash when peak_tmp < 0.75*cold_slab_chunk; only pick cublaslt if latency_gain > X and peak_tmp < 0.6*slab_free. Also a scoring function that includes peak_tmp/cluster_headroom would be cleaner.
Mike: I'll add telemetry hooks: chosen_kernel, peak_tmp_bytes, slab_free_at_choice, fallback_reason so we can alert on transient-risk.
Sarah: AB plan: control = old chooser; variant = transient_margin 0.55 + prefer_flash_for_seq_leq 2048. Collect OOMs, tail latency, kv-eviction churn for 1h.
Lee: action items:
- Evan: monitor hotfix 10% rollout & post OOMs/alerts (ETA 30m)
- Sarah: run AB analysis & recommend thresholds after 1h
- Mike: add telemetry + dashboard panels
- Toni: prototype scoring function PR and perf eval
Infra-bot: rollout status: 10% -> healthy
Evan: no OOMs in cohort so far, tail latency ~+2% for seq=2048 :thumbsup:
Sarah: if 1h looks good we'll ramp to 50% and watch KV eviction churn
Evan: opening follow-up RFC for scoring function + tmp_slab reserve proposal. Will update channel with metrics.
